arms.name: AI-allowed
arms.description: Any generative AI tool permitted while learning and writing the Session One essay; a dedicated logged-in ChatGPT account was provided. Standard online resources were also available. The Session Two essay prohibited AI and all external resources (PDF pp. 8-10; Figure A2, PDF p. 53). Arm counts describe assigned sign-ups and Session One participants, not the outcome-specific essay samples.

arms.name: AI-forbidden
arms.description: Generative AI prohibited during Session One; standard online resources including Google, Wikipedia, and the college library website were permitted. The Session Two essay prohibited all external resources (PDF pp. 8-10; Figure A2, PDF p. 53). Arm counts describe assigned sign-ups and Session One participants.

studies.task: Middlebury undergraduates learned about an assigned technical topic and wrote an analytical essay, then wrote an essay on a complementary prompt about the same topic without AI or external resources one week later (PDF pp. 7-10; Appendix B.2, PDF pp. 70-72).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (GPT-4o); any generative AI tool was permitted
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 2.1, Treatment; experiment conducted in Spring 2025, PDF p. 10, Section 3.1. Model release year is not printed.

preregistration.where: AEA RCT Registry, AEARCTR-0015806 (PDF p. 1); the pre-analysis plan is described in Section 3.4 (PDF p. 13). The registration was not independently retrieved.
preregistration.primary_outcome: The overall essay quality rating and the average quality index are explicitly described as the pre-analysis plan primary essay-based outcomes (PDF p. 13); the within-group similarity outcomes are not among them.

estimates.outcome: Within-group similarity, Session One essays (with AI)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Each student receives the average pairwise cosine similarity of their essay embedding with all other essays in the same treatment x topic x prompt cell. The paper names a sentence-embedding model fine-tuned from MPNet, citing Reimers and Gurevych and Song et al.; it does not identify the exact checkpoint. One essay per participant per session is summarized into a participant-level outcome (PDF p. 14, Section 3.4; PDF p. 41, Table 5 notes).

regression.model: Intent-to-treat OLS regression of the student-level mean within-group cosine similarity on AI-access assignment, with Session One time-slot fixed effects and double-lasso-selected controls (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 3.3; PDF p. 41, Table 5 notes).

paper_effect.standardizer: None: raw cosine-similarity units. This is the printed TOT (instrumental-variable) coefficient, not a standardized effect; see notes.

estimates.notes: The ITT coefficient and robust standard error are stored in regression. paper_effect.type=other stores the paper's additional treatment-on-the-treated (TOT) coefficient and robust standard error in raw cosine-similarity units, estimated by two-stage least squares using randomized access as the instrument for actual ChatGPT use; it is not a standardized effect. The two estimands concern the same arm contrast and are kept in this outcome record. Signs are transcribed as similarity, so higher values indicate less diversity. The paper prints a control mean but no treatment-arm mean, arm SDs, arm-mean SEs, exact p-value, test statistic, or numeric confidence limits for this outcome. The AI-arm analysis count is not printed separately and has not been obtained by subtraction. The analysis uses student-level robust SEs; no adjustment for dependence between scores sharing essays or clustering by lab/time slot is reported. Figures 6 and A7 (PDF pp. 34 and 58) plot standardized similarity effects and confidence intervals without numerical effect or endpoint labels; no values were read from graph positions. Section 4.3 also describes the Session One effect as a 0.5 percent change relative to the control mean; this percentage is transcribed from the prose, not calculated. outcome_with_ai denotes access in the AI-allowed arm, regardless of actual take-up.

open_items: Neither session's AI-arm mean similarity is printed; Table 5 reports control means and adjusted ITT/TOT coefficients. Arm levels cannot be completed by adding an adjusted coefficient to an unadjusted control mean.
The paper does not print similarity SDs, arm-mean SEs, exact p-values, or numeric confidence limits. Standardized effects and intervals in Figures 6 and A7 are graphical only.
The AI-arm essay-analysis count is not printed separately in either session. n_treatment remains null; the printed total and control counts are retained without subtraction.
The precise MPNet-based embedding checkpoint and the number of essay pairs entering the similarities are not stated.

Complete accounting of missing essays is not provided for the similarity analyses. The September paper's Table 5 gives the outcome-specific counts, and its Table A4 has matching writing-style counts; the earlier screening form's July table-count conflict is not carried into this version.
No covariance or cluster correction for shared essays in the similarity averages is reported; the retained uncertainty is the paper's student-level heteroskedasticity-robust uncertainty.
The GPT-4o release year is not printed in the paper; ai_tool.year is null.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-09. Rule 6 limits c750 to within-group essay similarity in Session One and unaided Session Two. This extraction uses only the specified September PDF for numerical evidence; the supplied July markdown was read completely as a coverage map and its results were not substituted for September values. The entire September PDF, including figures, tables, references, and Appendices A-D, was read with PyMuPDF; the Table 5 row was also checked with find_tables. PDF page indices plus one equal printed page numbers for the cited pages. is_own_paper follows codebook Review 1 decision 7. Study and arm n_analyzed fields describe Session One attendees across study analyses, whereas estimates use the printed outcome-specific samples. The label ITT is retained from the paper even though analyses use attendees with available outcomes rather than all assigned sign-ups. Students were randomized to computers in parallel labs within time slots, then each lab was assigned its condition; individual assignment follows the screening form and the explicit seat randomization, and no independently printed per-arm cluster count is supplied. Repeated sessions do not constitute a crossover or paired AI-condition comparison. The analytical essay is coded task_type=other, as in the screening form; eligibility comes from cross-writer similarity. No explicit shared-participant claim with another paper is stated. Each outcome record keeps ITT in regression and the additional raw TOT result in paper_effect (type other), so there are two outcome records rather than duplicate records for the two estimands. No means, sample counts, standardized effects, standard errors, intervals, or test statistics were calculated.
